events.factual_description: Suntory Hall presents two performances of Yo-Yo Ma's 40th Anniversary Special Concert in the Main Hall on Sunday, October 25 and Tuesday, October 27, 2026. Both performances begin at 19:00 with doors at 18:20; the date range in this record represents those two announced concert dates and does not imply an October 26 performance. The program opens with Shostakovich's Piano Trio No. 2 in E minor, Op. 67, performed by Ma, violinist Keila Wakao and pianist Yun Janice Lu, followed by the eighth movement from Messiaen's Quatuor pour la fin du temps with Ma and Lu. The second part is Wisdom for a Broken World, curated by Jeremy Dutcher, with Ma, Dutcher, OKI on vocals and tonkori, and MAREWREW on vocals. Suntory Hall's primary announcement states that Ma performed in the hall's 1986 opening series and frames these concerts as part of the hall's 40th Anniversary Programme. Listed prices are ¥27,000 (S), ¥22,000 (A), ¥17,000 (B), ¥12,000 (C), and ¥3,000 for eligible U25 tickets.

priority_review.rationale: Concrete scarcity: Yo-Yo Ma appeared in Suntory Hall's 1986 opening series and is returning for the hall's one-time 40th-anniversary programme with a specially constructed Shostakovich/Messiaen-to-Wisdom for a Broken World arc, the latter curated by Jeremy Dutcher with Ainu artists OKI and MAREWREW. That exact anniversary, institutional history and cultural configuration cannot recur as another 40th anniversary. A+ would understate the genuine-regret-if-missed character of missing the Tokyo engagement entirely. S+ would overstate scarcity because the same program is presented twice in Tokyo and Ma/Dutcher are also performing related Asia-tour dates.

en.why_it_matters: The anniversary is doing real musical work here. Yo-Yo Ma played Suntory Hall's opening series in 1986 and returns forty years later with a program that moves from Shostakovich and Messiaen into Jeremy Dutcher's Wisdom for a Broken World, where Wolastoqiyik perspective meets OKI's tonkori and MAREWREW's Ainu voices. The reason to care is not Ma's fame by itself; it is the way one of the world's defining cellists, a hall with forty years of shared history, and Indigenous musical traditions are being placed in the same deliberately constructed evening.
en.trip_verdict: If a Tokyo/Kanto stay overlaps October 25 or 27, protect one of the two nights and build the evening around Suntory Hall. The duplicate performance dates create useful flexibility: choose the one that fits the trip rather than sacrificing another singular Kanto night simply to attend both.
en.listen_before: Yo-Yo Ma — Notes for the Future; Yo-Yo Ma & Jeremy Dutcher — Honor Song

es.why_it_matters: Aquí el aniversario sí forma parte de la música. Yo-Yo Ma tocó en la serie inaugural de Suntory Hall en 1986 y vuelve cuarenta años después con un programa que pasa de Shostakóvich y Messiaen a Wisdom for a Broken World, concebido por Jeremy Dutcher, donde la perspectiva wolastoqiyik se encuentra con el tonkori de OKI y las voces ainu de MAREWREW. La razón para estar en RADAR no es la fama de Ma por sí sola: es esa combinación deliberada entre uno de los grandes violonchelistas vivos, una sala con cuarenta años de historia compartida y tradiciones musicales indígenas dentro de una misma noche.
es.trip_verdict: Si una estancia en Tokio/Kanto coincide con el 25 o el 27 de octubre, protegería una de las dos noches y armaría la velada alrededor de Suntory Hall. Tener dos funciones da margen para escoger la que mejor encaje sin sacrificar otro one-off realmente singular en Kanto sólo por intentar asistir a ambas.
